context: extending the ovoid-defect programme from q=3 to q=5, where the objects are 156 points and 156 lines instead of 40 and 40

tau1.question: tau_1(W(3,5)) = 28 or 29?
tau1.publishedSource: Eisfeld, Storme, Szonyi, Sziklai, Discrete Math 238 (2001) 35-51: a cover of Q(4,q), q odd, needs more than q^2+1+(q-1)/3; at q=5 that is >27.33, so >=28
tau1.note: the published bound is TIGHT at q=3, where it gives >=11 and tau_1 = 11 exactly. Whether it is tight at q=5 is open here.

ovoidDeficiency.question: def(5) = fewest lines missed by a 26-set
ovoidDeficiency.lowerBoundReason: W(3,5) has no ovoid (Thas, q odd), so def >= 1
ovoidDeficiency.note: def(3) = 3 is OPTIMAL; whether def(q) = q is neither shown nor refuted

productBound.question: is B x B beatable for W(3,5), as it is for W(3,3)?
productBound.why: 814 beats 841 = 29^2 but loses to 784 = 28^2, and tau_1(W(3,5)) is undecided in [28,29], so no claim can be made. Beating 784 would make it unconditional.

boundary: all four questions here are open. Nothing in this file supports a general theorem that a positive ovoid defect makes the product construction beatable; that remains a q=3 fact only.
